chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Hammad ibn Isa and Fadalah and Safwan, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who visited the House (Kaaba) and did not cease from his tawaf, supplication, and sa'i, and supplication, until the dawn rose. He said: 'There is no penalty upon him, for he was in obedience to Allah, Exalted and Glorious.'

And the other case is that he may have left Mina after half the night, for whenever he leaves after the completion of the first half for the visitation, nothing is obligatory upon him, although it is preferable that he does not leave until morning. That is indicated by what was narrated:

key_terms.السَّعْيِ: His walking between Safa and Marwa (Sa'i)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who performs Hajj rituals continuously through the night until dawn?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, highlighting the juristic distinction between the obligatory minimum of staying in Mina (until sunset) and the recommended practice of remaining until dawn. The hadith clarifies that continuous worship through the night exempts the pilgrim from penalty, while leaving after the first half of the night is permissible but less virtuous, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing legal minimums with spiritual excellence (fada'il).
